title: Sample 17-10: Syllabified Words in a Spelling Activity

illustrates.quote: a. Do not divide a syllabified word between lines unless it is too long to fit on a single line. If a word is divided between lines, it must be at a syllable break. (See Sample 17-10: Syllabified Words in a Spelling Activity on page 17-23.)

print.notes: A cell-5 heading, then a numbered list of three syllable-division rules, each with two hyphen-joined, wholly-uncontracted example words in parentheses.
print.printFeatures: Italicised heading; a numbered rules list (1. 2. 3.).

braille.notes: A's braille.lines kept (matches source exactly, including the trailing blank content line, source line 14091); B dropped it.

resolution: Both runs (A, B) came from the same model (Gemini Pro via Antigravity, 17 Sep 2026) and are not independent; agreement was treated as no evidence. braille.lines independently re-extracted from references/_text/braille-formats-2016.txt (the line-number field, digits + >=3 spaces, or the fixed left margin measured in ASCII spaces before any U+2800 cell, stripped by counting; U+2800->space; trailing spaces removed). Braille: A's version (trailing blank, source-verified) kept over B's. illustrates.rule: corrected to '17.8.1a' — this exact sample is the one the source itself cross-references by name at the end of clause a ('If a word is divided between lines... (See Sample 17-10...)'); both runs' own bare '17.8.1'/'17.8.1' is less precise. Modeled as a lettered list; each example word wholly uncontracted (17.8.1). EXPECT PARTIAL: standards-map.md (BANA 17.8.1a) already confirms a space-syllabified word wraps correctly at the syllable break (wrapCells only breaks at a space), but a HYPHEN-joined syllabified word with no spaces (e.g. 'brink-man-ship') does NOT — wrapCells' hard-chunk fallback has no hyphen awareness, splitting mid-syllable instead. Print description corrected 23 Sep 2026 (see printCorrections).

printCorrections.evidence: references/_gemini/_done/gold-17-A/page-487.png: the printed list is numbered "1. Divide between 2 consonants (rab-bit, mon-key)", "2. ...", "3. ...". Braille lines 2/4/6 begin #A4 #B4 #C4 (number sign + digit + period), i.e. numerals, matching the print.
